summary: Frontend-only behavioral check that ESC closes modals across the admin app via the new shared useEscape() hook. Logged in as admin (admin@attendance.app), verified three distinct modals/overlays and the blur-then-close semantics. All checks passed.

tests_performed.case: Members > New Member modal (data-testid='member-form') closes on ESC when no input focused
Focused text input inside member-form: 1st ESC blurs input and modal stays open (activeElement went INPUT -> BODY, modal still in DOM)
2nd ESC after blur closes member-form modal
ESC with NO modal open is a no-op (URL unchanged, no navigation, no crash)
LeaveReportPrompt reliably dismissible via ESC on multiple pages (home, members, meal-entry)

critical_code_review_comments: useEscape.js correctly uses a module-level stack so only the top-most modal closes per ESC; good design.
The listener uses stopPropagation() only when actually closing a modal — safe default so native ESC behavior (closing <dialog>, native file pickers, etc.) is preserved when stack is empty.

Minor: the keydown listener is attached once and never removed (module-scoped `listenerAttached`). Fine in practice but worth noting for SSR / test isolation; it is already guarded by `typeof window !== 'undefined'`.

Only inputs/textarea/select/contentEditable are treated as 'blur first'. Shadcn/Radix comboboxes with role='combobox' on a BUTTON will NOT get the blur-first treatment and will directly close the modal — acceptable but a subtle UX asymmetry.

Did not spot-check every one of the ~20 modals listed; representative coverage (LeaveReportPrompt + MemberForm) exercises the hook's full behavior (open, stack push, blur-first, close, cleanup, no-op when empty).
seed_data_creation: None. Modals were opened and dismissed via ESC without saving.
